english: Addition” v | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget FOREWORD This year would undoubtedly go down as one of the most challenging in the economic history of our country.

twi: Sɛdeɛ ɛkɔɔ so wɔ ewiase aman ahodoɔ soɔ no, yadeɛ kontonkurowi COVID-19 to hyɛɛ yɛn so wɔ afe 2020 ɔfa a ɛdi kan no mu ma sikadwuma tɔɔ ape nam so ma sika a ɛba ɔman fotoɔ mu no so teeɛ na afei nso yɛbɔɔ ɛka a na yɛn ani nna de ko tiaa yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi.
english: Like the rest of the world, we were hit with the COVID-19 pandemic in the first quarter of 2020, which resulted in a slowdown in economic activity, leading to a reduction in our revenues and unbudgeted additional costs associated with fighting the pandemic.

twi: Ɛberɛ a yɛhyɛɛ aseɛ tuu Nsakraeɛ Pa Nhyehyɛeɛ ho anammɔn na yɛsusuu sɛ afei deɛ, yɛrebɔ yɛn ho mmɔden ade yɛn ho afiri yadeɛ kontonkurowi yi ho nsunsuansoɔ mu ara pɛ na ɔhaw afoforɔ bɛbɔɔ mu a, ɛnam so ama nneɛma a ɛma sikasɛm gyina yie a yɛde totoo yie firi afe 2017 kɔsi 2019 mu no nyinaa asane agye agu. Deɛ ɛdi kan yɛ Russia ne Ukraine ɔko no, deɛ ɛdi hɔ nso yɛ ɛberɛ a yɛsɛee wɔ akwanhodoɔ a yɛbɛfa so anya sika wɔ 2022 sikasɛm nhyehyɛeɛ mu no nnyetom ho a, ɛnam so maa amansan boseabɔfoɔ de too edwa sɛ yɛmfata sɛ wɔbɔ yɛn bosea.
english: Just when we thought, we were making great strides in our recovery from the damaging effects of the pandemic by the commencement of the implementation of our transformation agenda, we were hit with a variety of events which have over the period, eroded the macroeconomic successes we chalked from 2017 to 2019. First it was the Russia-Ukraine war, then a delay in the passage of key revenue measures in the 2022 budget, which led to credit rating downgrades.

twi: Afei, bɛyɛ mfeɛ edu nie, prɛko pɛ Amansan Boseabɔ ho Edwadifoɔ mpɛ sɛ wɔbɛma yɛn bosea, ɔman yi ara mu boseabɔ ho nsɛm nso bɛyɛɛ basaa ma nsiho boɔ kɔɔ soro pa ara na ɛnam so ma boseabɔ ho ɛka kɔɔ soro a, ama yɛn sika mu duru no kɔ ara na ɛrekɔ fam.
english: Suddenly, for the first time in ten years, the International Capital Market was closed to us, domestic financing conditions tightened and the cost of borrowing increased, contributing to high debt service and the rapid depreciation of the cedi.

twi: Yei kyerɛ sɛ, ɛberɛ a amannɔne sika a yɛnya firi amansan boseabɔ edwa so ne sika a ɛfiri adwadeɛ a yɛde kɔ amannɔne mu no so reteɛ, na afei ɛsiane sɛdeɛ yɛpɛ amannɔne nneɛma pa ara enti, sika a yɛde kra nneɛma firi amannɔne no nso kɔ ara na ɛrekɔ soro, na amannɔne ɛka a yɛde no nso kɔ ara na ɛrekɔ soro no, na yɛn sika mu duru no so te ara na ɛreteɛ.
english: Thus, even as the foreign currency support from the capital market and our foreign earnings declined, the rise in our import bill rose from our apparent insatiable demand for imports as a country, coupled with our increasing debt servicing bill, further undermined the value of our currency.

twi: Yei ama asetena mu ayɛ den ama Aban ne ankorankoro nyinaa.
english: This has led to a high cost of living for us all, both as Government and as individuals.

twi: Fango boɔ a ɛgu so rekɔ soro enti, ama nneɛma boɔ ayɛ den a bosome Ahineme mu wɔ afe 2022 mu, nneɛma-boɔ-sorokɔ kɔduruu ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduanan ne akyire pɔ ɛnan (40.4% in October 2022).
english: Rising fuel prices have led to increases in prices of most goods and services, with inflation at an all high of 40.4% in October 2022.

twi: Yɛakɔ nsɔhwɛ a ano yɛ den pa ara mu na Aban nim ɔhaw a saa tebea yi de abɛto mo so.
english: We have been really tested as a people, and Government empathises greatly with you for the undue pressures this has brought.

english: Addition” vi | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget Traders Association, Academia, Think-Tanks, and the ordinary Ghanaians who continue to bear with us even as we navigate these difficult times.

twi: Megyina Ɔmanpanin Nana Addo Danquah Akuffo-Addo anan mu hyɛ Ghanafoɔ nyinaa bɔ sɛ Aban reyɛ nhyehyɛeɛ ahodoɔ a ɛbɛboa ama nneɛma a ɛma ɔman sikasɛm gyina yie no ase atim na ama ɔman sikasɛm asane apagya, yɛatumi anya sika agu ɔman fotoɔ mu, yɛde aban nnwuma mu nsakraeɛ ho anammɔntuo adi dwuma, yɛatrɛ abɛɛfo mfidie ne dwumadie ho akwanhodoɔ mu, yɛate amannɔne nneɛma a ɛho nhia a yɛkra ba ɔman yi mu no so, yɛayɛ adwadeɛ a yɛde kɔ amannɔne dodoɔ, yɛatrɛ ɔman yi mu adwadeɛyɛ nnwuma mu a wɔbɛyɛ adwadeɛ a yɛkra firi amannɔne no bi wɔ ɔman yi ara mu na afei yɛabɔ mmɔborɔwafoɔ ne wɔn a wɔayi wɔn totwene wɔ asetenam no ho ban.
english: Nana Addo Danquah Akuffo-Addo, I want to assure all Ghanaians that Government is putting in place polices that will reset the economy and restore macroeconomic stability, raise significant revenues, implement structural and public reforms, expand digital and physical infrastructure, reduce nonessential imports, promote exports, expand local production of import substitute, and protect the vulnerable and socially excluded.

twi: Osuahunu a yɛanya afiri tebea a yɛwɔ mu saa ɛberɛ yi mu no ama yɛahunu sɛ ɛhia pa ara sɛ yɛyɛ nsakraeɛ de sesa ɔman yi sikasɛm na ɛtumi gyina afebɔɔ.
english: The lessons we have learnt as a country from this period have made it necessary for us to permanently restructure and transform our economy and build resilience.

twi: Yɛbɛsane agyina yɛn nan so.
english: We will come out of this stronger.

twi: Awurade bɛka yɛn ho na wama yɛn ahoɔden a yɛde bɛtu anammɔn yi.

english: Addition” 1 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget INTRODUCTION 1. The 2023 Citizen’s Budget is a summary of what Government achieved in 2022 and how much it intends to collect and utilise its revenues to implement policies and programmes.

twi: Asɛntire a ɛda Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ yi so ne “Yɛreka abom adi dwuma de Mpontuo ne Adwadeɛyɛ asane ama ahoɔden aba Ɔman Sikasɛm mu na yɛama aseɛ atim”.
english: The theme of the budget is “Restoring and Sustaining Macroeconomic Stability and Resilience for Inclusive Growth & Value Addition”.

twi: Mfeɛ a abɛsene korɔ no, ɛrekame ayɛ sɛ Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ foforɔ biara a yɛbɛyɛ no, yɛhyehyɛ mpontunnwuma foforɔ a yɛbɛyɛ wɔ mu a, yɛyi yɛn ani firi deɛ ɛrekɔ soɔ no so.
english: Over the years, every new budget invariably contains a host of new projects to be initiated at the expense of ongoing projects.

twi: Ɛnyɛ ahokyere nko ara na saa tebea no de ba yɛn sikasɛm so na mmom ama ɔman yi da so tua ɛka wɔ mpontunnwuma ho a ama mpontunnwuma ho ɛka akɔ soro pa ara ɛsiane sɛ ɛka a anka ɛsɛ sɛ yɛtua a yɛatu ahyɛ ɛda no wɔ nsiho wɔ ho a, ɛno nso kɔ soro.
english: This does not only put pressure on our finances but has also historically resulted in payment of arrears which raise the overall cost of projects as the deferred payments attract interest cost.

twi: Afe 2023 mu no, Aban bɛyɛ nhyehyɛeɛ ne dwumadie afoforɔ, nanso yɛbɛhwɛ sɛ ɛbɛyɛ yɛn asɛnhia na yɛawie mpontunnwuma ahodoɔ a ɛrekɔ soɔ no nyinaa.
english: In 2023, Government will implement new policies and programmes, but will also encourage the culture of completing all existing projects.

english: These developments have manifested through rapid exchange rate depreciation, high inflation, unsustainable debt service burden, fiscal stress and external sector shocks despite the monetary and fiscal policy interventions instituted by Government.

Saa ɔfa yi da mmɔden a Aban rebɔ fa dwumadie sononko (government flagship projects) a ɔhyɛɛ aseɛ wɔ asoɛeɛ ahodoɔ mu wɔ afe 2022 mu no ho ne mpontunnwuma a wahyehyɛ (planned activities) sɛ ɔbɛdi wɔ afe 2023 mu no adi.
english: Addition” 13 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget SECTORAL DEVELOPMENT AND OUTLOOK 25. This section highlights the performance of government flagship projects in the key sectors in 2022 and planned activities for implementation in 2023.

twi: Saa dwumadie ne anammɔn ahodoɔ yi nyinaa gyina Aban Animanim yi ara mu Ɔman Mpontuo Dwumadie Nhyehyɛeɛ (Government’s Medium-Term National Development Policy Framework, 2022-2026) no so.
english: These programmes and activities are based primarily on Government’s Medium-Term National Development Policy Framework (2022-2026).

twi: Dwumadie ahodoɔ yi botaeɛ ne sɛ ɛbɛboa ama Aban atumi aduru botaeɛ ahodoɔ a ɛfa Ghana COVID 19 ne Ankorankorɛ Nnwuma mu Nkanyan ho Mmoa (Ghanacares) ho no ne anammɔntuo a ɛwɔ Apam a wɔayɛ afa nhyehyɛeɛ a ɛwɔ Amanaman Nkabom Ekuo Mpontuo nhyehyɛeɛ (UN Agenda 2030, SDG’s) ne Abibirem Nkabom Kuo Botaeɛ 2023 (African Union Agenda 2063) mu ho no ho.
english: The programme aims to attain the objectives under Government CARES Programmes as well as targets arising from our international commitments with regards to the UN Agenda 2030 (SDG’s) and African Union Agenda 2063.

twi: Saa ɔfa yi da Aban mmɔden a wabɔ wɔ Ɔman yi mmeaeɛ ne Asoɛeɛ ahodoɔ mu wɔ afe 2022 mu ne dwuma a ɔbɛdi wɔ afe 2023 mu adi.
english: This section highlights the performance of Government in key areas and sectors of the economy in 2022, as well as programmes and activities for implementation in 2023.

twi: Aduane Ho Banbɔ 28. Aban botaeɛ a ɛsi náni so sɛ ɔbɛma nnua mfudeɛ (tree ɔrops) ho mfasoɔ adɔɔso enti no, ɔmaa akuafoɔ nsa kaa ɛho ntutɛ nnua nketewa dodoɔ Ɔpepem mmienu ne ahanson (2.7 million) wɔ afe 2022 wɔ kuayɛ ɛberɛ no mu.
english: Food Security 28. Government in line with its agenda to vary earnings from the Tree Crops subsector provided 2.7 million improved seedlings to farmers during the 2022 cropping season.

twi: Aban gyinaa Mmoayɛn A Ɛde Nnuane ne Nnwuma Ba Nhyehyɛeɛ (Rearing for Food and Jobs module) no so tɔɔ nkokɔbedeɛ dodoɔ mpem ɔha aduonu (120,000) kyekyɛ maa mmaa nkokɔyɛn akuafoɔ dodoɔ apem (1000) a wɔwɔ Nkuropɔn, Nkuro ne Mansini ahodoɔ nkron (9 MMDAs) mu a wɔn ne (Savelugu, Sagnarigu, Wa Municipal, Nandom, Sissala Apueeɛ, Krachi Apueeɛ, Nkwanta Anafoɔ, Techiman Atifi ne Nkoranza).
english: 29. 120,000-layer birds were procured and distributed to 1,000 female poultry farmers in 9 MMDAs (Savelugu, Sagnarigu, Wa Municipal, Nandom, Sissala East, Krachi East, Nkwanta South, Techiman North and Nkoranza) under the Rearing for Food and Jobs module.

twi: 24 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ dwuma (120-capacity poultry battery cage) a wɔde nkokɔ no bɛgu mu.
english: Beneficiaries also received a 120-capacity poultry battery cage to house the birds.

twi: Deɛ ɛka ho bio ne sɛ, yɛtotɔɔ ntɔtemmoa nketewa (small ruminants) dodoɔ mpem mmiɛnsa ahanson aduonum (3,750) kyekyɛ kɔɔ mmeaeɛ a wɔyɛn ntɔtemmoa a ɛyɛ akuafoɔ aduanan enum (45) bi dea de sɔɔ wɔn asene sɛdeɛ ɛbɛte mfudeɛ ho ɔhaw a wɔhyia no so so nam so aboa ama wɔatumi ayɛ wɔn asetena mu asɛdeɛ ahodoɔ.
english: In addition, a total of 3,750 small ruminants were procured and distributed to livestock breeding stations and 45 farmers to strengthen their resilience to shocks from crop failure and maintain households ability to fulfil social obligations

twi: Afe 2023 mu, Aban bɛhwɛ ama wɔadua, na wɔakyekyɛ ateaa (cashew), nkuto (shea), kube(coconut), abɛ (oil palm), mamgoo (mango), ne rɔba (rubber) dodoɔ ɔpepem enum ne aduosia enum (5.65million) a ɛso dɔsɔɔ de ama akuafoɔ dodoɔ mpem ɔha aduɔson enum ( 175,000).
english: In 2023, Government, will facilitate the production and distribution of 5.65 million high-quality planting materials of Addition” 14 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget cashew, shea, coconut, oil palm, mango, and rubber to 175,000 tree crop farmers.

twi: Afe 2022 mu no, Aban gyinaa “Mansini Baako Adekoradan Baako Nhyehyɛeɛ (“One District One Warehouse” programme) no so wiee mfudeɛ adekoradan dodoɔ aduosia enum (65 warehouses) nam so de mɛtrik tɔn dodoɔ mpem aduɔwɔtwe kaa ɔman ahoɔden a yɛde kora aburoo sɛso nnuane no ho, sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyi nnɔbaeɛ a wɔtwa a ɛsɛe kwa no afiri hɔ, ama akuafoɔ nsa aka wɔn adwuma no ho mfasoɔ.
english: Government in 2022, completed 65 warehouses which added 80,000mt to the national grain storage capacity under the “One District One Warehouse” programme to address the persistent problem of post-harvest losses, and secure farmer income.

twi: Afe 2023 mu no, Aban bɛwie Tamne afuo-so-nsuguguo dwumadie no ɔfa a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa no, atutu asutaeɛ wɔ Sunyeri, Tousal/Jeyiri, Tasundo ne Gilang na yɛatutu afuo-so-nsuguguo mmena wɔ mmeaeɛ afoforɔ a ɛbɛyɛ yie Vunania and Gilang.
english: In 2023, Government will complete Phase III of Tamne Irrigation Project, construct dams at Sunyeri, Tousal/Jeyiri, Tasundo and Gilang and develop irrigable areas at Vunania and Gilang.

twi: Ɔyɛasaseyie a wɔmfraa mu ho anammɔntuo 34. Ɛsiane sɛdeɛ nnansa yi ɔyɛasaseyie a wɔafra mu (inorgani fertiliser) ho yɛɛ den ma ne ɛboɔ nso kɔɔ soro pa ara ɛsiane ewiase nyinaa mu ɔhaw a ɛrekɔ so no enti no, Aban apagya adwadifoɔ a wɔtɔn ɔyɛasaseyie a wɔmfraa mu (Organiɔ fertiliser) no kyɛfa a wɔwɔ mu sɛdeɛ ɛmma dodoɔ a ɛbɛhia no ntɔ sini.
english: Promotion of organic Fertilizer 34. Given the recent disruption in inorganic fertiliser supply chains and sharp increases in prices from the global crisis, Government has increased the quota for organic fertiliser suppliers to cover the shortfall in supply of inorganic fertilisers.

twi: Saa anammɔntuo yi aboa ama kuayɛ akɔ nkan, ayi ɛkɔm afiri hɔ.
english: This initiative has improved food production and decreases the threat to food security.

twi: Afe 2023 mu no, Aban bɛgye mmoa afiri EXIM sikakorabea (EXIM bank) no hɔ nam so asisi mfidie a wɔde yɛ ɔyɛasaseyie a wɔmfaa mu no bi afoforɔ, asane atrɛtrɛ deɛ ɛwɔ hɔ dada no mu.
english: In 2023, Government will facilitate the establishment and expansion of local organic fertilizer production plants with support from the EXIM bank.

twi: Afe 2022 mu no, Aban gyinaa dwumadie a wɔato edin Nsuomnamyɛn a ɛma Nnuane ne Nnwuma nhyehyɛeɛ (Aquaculture for Food and Jobs, AFJ) no so, hyehyɛɛ nsuomnam adekoradeɛ dodoɔ ɔha aduonu ɛnan (124 holding facilities)nsuomnam asutaeɛ ɔha ne nwɔtwe ne nsuomnam ebuo edu nsia (108 ponds and 16 cages), maa nsuomnam aduane baage dodoɔ mpem Dunson, ahanan aduosia (17, 460,) sane de nsuomnam mma guguu akuo ne nnwuma ahodoɔ dodoɔ aduonu enum asutaeɛ ne akoradeɛ mu.
english: In 2022, Government under the Aquaculture for Food and Jobs (AFJ) Programme, constructed 124 holding facilities (108 ponds and 16 cages), provided 17,460 bags of fish feed, as well as stocked ponds and cages with fingerlings to 25 beneficiary institutions and groups.

twi: Bio, yɛmaa nnipa dodoɔ ahanu aduonu ɛnan (294) nteteeɛ fa ɛkwan pa a yɛfa so yɛ kua ho, ɛnna nsuomnam akuafoɔ ahanan ne nwɔtwe (408) nso, yɛmaa wɔn nteteeɛ faa ɛkwan a yɛfa so yɛ nsuomnam aduane wɔ ɔman yi mu ho.
english: In addition, 294 beneficiaries were trained in fish farming practices while 408 fish farmers also received training in the formulation and preparation of local fish feed

twi: Afe 2023 mu no, Aban bɛma akuhodoɔ bi nsa aka asutaeɛ a wɔde kley na anwono dodoɔ ahasa (300 earthen ponds), nsuomnam adekoradeɛ aduanan (40 cages) tapolin tanke aduonum mmienu (52 tarpaulin tanks) na wasane de nsuomnam aduane baage dodoɔ mpem aduasa enum ( 35,000), koobi (tilapia) ne adwene mma (catfish) ɔpepem mmiɛnsa (3 million) ama wɔn.
english: In 2023, Government will provide 300 earthen ponds, 40 cages and 52 tarpaulin tanks and supply 35,000 bags of fish feed, 3 million tilapia and catfish fingerlings to 50 beneficiary groups.

twi: Kookoo ho Dwumadie 38. Kookoo dwumadie mu no, yɛmaa mmabunu dii dwuma ahodoɔ sɛ ebia nsiesie (rehabilitation), kookoo a yɛtwa gu sane dua (replanting), kookoo so adupeteɛ (mass spraying), ɔyɛasaseyie peteɛ (fertilizer application), ne kookoo nnua dodoɔ ho twitwa (mass pruning) so maa mmabunu dodoɔ mpem ɔha aduanan nson (147,000) nyaa adwuma yɛeɛ de sii akuraase kɔ kuro kɛseɛ mu akwantuo no ano.
english: Addition” 15 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget Cocoa Sector 38. Under the cocoa sector, 147,000 jobs were created through the implementation of various programmes such as rehabilitation, replanting, mass spraying, fertilizer application, and mass pruning to direct youthful energies into productive ventures and reduce rural-urban migration.

twi: 26 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ 39. Afe 2023 mu no, Aban bɛtoa dwumadie ahodoɔ yi so, nam so ama nnwuma aba, ama deɛ ɛwɔ hɔ dada no ase atim, nam so ate asodie a ɛda aban so fa nnwuma a ɛnni hɔ no so.
english: In 2023, government will continue implementation of these programmes, to create additional jobs and consolidate the already created jobs to lessen the unemployment burden on Government.

twi: Ogyahoɔden 40. Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na yɛbɛsi ogyahoɔden a yɛhwere wɔ ɛberɛ a yɛde anyinam ahoɔden rekɔ mmeammea a ɛhia wɔ ne kyɛ mu ano na ɛho nhyehyɛeɛ nyinaa bɛkɔ nkan enti no, yɛwiee, Firaw Mantam- Achimota anyinam ahoma ho dwumadie (161kV Volta-Achimota- Mallam Transmission Line Upgrade) no.
english: Energy 40. In order to reduce transmission and distribution system losses and improve transmission system reliability, the 161kV Volta- Achimota-Mallam Transmission Line Upgrade Project was completed and is in operation.

twi: Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na ɛnnuru afe 2024 no na Anyinam ahoɔden aduru Ɔman yi afanan nyinaa no enti, Ɛbɔ 2022 mu no, yɛtwaa mpɔtam dodoɔ ɔha aduonum nson (157) too Ɔman Anyinam ahoɔden nhoma no so bi nam so pagyaa anyinam ahoɔden akwannya a ɛwɔ ɔman yi mu no mu firi afe 2021 mu deɛ ɔha nkyɛmu aduɔwɔtwe nson akyiri pɔ mmiɛnsa (87.03%) no kɔduru ɔha aduɔwɔtwe nwɔtwe akyiri pɔ aduonum ɛnan (88.54%).
english: In line with Government’s vision to achieve universal coverage of electricity by 2024, 157 communities were connected to the national grid as of September 2022, increasing the national electricity access rate from 87.03 percent in 2021 to 88.54 percent.

twi: Aban botaeɛ a ɛne sɛ ɔbɛma anyinam akɔ nkuro a nsuo atwa ho ahyia (supɔ) na ɛhɔ kɔ yɛ den no enti, yɛafiri aseɛ asisi ɛho mfidie mmiɛnsa wɔ Azizkpe, Aflive ne Alorkpem a ɛwɔ Ada Apueeɛ Mansini a ɛwɔ Nkran Mantam mu no mu.
english: As part of Government’s strategy to electrify island communities and hard-to-reach areas with renewable energy technologies, civil works on the construction of three mini-grids at Azizkpe, Aflive and Alorkpem Islands in the Ada East District of the Greater Accra Region have been completed.

twi: Afe 2023 mu no, Aban bɛdi dwuma nam so de ahoboa a ɔreyɛ wɔ Nkran-Kumasi anyinam nhoma ne Atɔeɛ fam anyinam nhoma nsiesie dwumadie ho no aba awieeɛ, na wasane aboa ama 27 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ dwumadie a wɔato edin sɛ “Aban De Owia mu Anyinam Di Dwumadi “no afiri aseɛ.
english: Addition” 16 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget 43. In 2023, Government will work to finalise preparations towards the Accra-Kumasi transmission line, the Western Corridor Transmission Upgrade Project as well as support the "Government Goes Solar" project for implementation.

twi: Aban bɛgyina nhyehyɛeɛ a wɔato edin “SHEP-4”, “SHEP-5” ne “Turkey dwumadie” no so atwe anyinam nhoma akɔ nkuro ahanan (400) afoforɔ bi so wɔ afe 2023 mu. Nkuro ahodoɔ bi a ɛwɔ Ahafo, Asante, Bono, Atifi, ne Atifi Apueeɛ Amantam mu nsa bɛka bi.
english: Government will connect an additional 400 towns under the SHEP- 4, SHEP-5 and Turnkey Projects in 2023 including electrification in selected communities in Ahafo, Ashanti, Bono, Northern, and Upper East Regions.

twi: Aban bɛfiri aseɛ akyekyɛ abɛɛfo lɔre akwan ho owia mu anyinam nkanea no (all-in-one solar street lighting) akokɔ Nkuropɔn, Nkuro, ne Mansini ahodoɔ no mu.
english: Government will also commence the deployment of all-in-one solar street lighting in Metropolitan Municipal District Assemblies (MMDAs) across the country.

twi: 28 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ Adwumanya ho Nhyehyɛeɛ 45. Ɛduruu Ahineme 2022 mu no, na Mmabunu Adwumanya Adwumakuo (Youth Employment Agency) no, agyina ne nkorabata ahodoɔ no so afa nnipa dodoɔ Mpem aduɔwɔtwe, ahanson aduasa enum (80,735).
english: Employment Drive 45. As at October 2022, the Youth Employment Agency (YEA) had engaged 80,735 beneficiaries under its various modules.

twi: Afe 2022 mu, Aban faa Ɔman Adwumanya ho ɛkwan foforɔ nhyehyɛeɛ (National Alternative Employment and Livelihood Programme (NAELP); no so tuu anammɔn a ɛdidi soɔ yi: Siesiee nsase a asɛe, sane duaa nnua wɔ asase dodoɔ hɛkta ahansia aduanan enum (645) so nam so maa adwumanya ho akwannya dodoɔ mpem mmienu ahasa.; na afei Guu nnua aba dodoɔ ɔpepem aduonu (20 million) de boaa Afuoyɛ Mpontuo Dwumadie (plantation development programme) no nam so maa mmabunu mpem aduɔwɔtwe aduɔson baako (80,071) a wɔwɔ Akotom, Adinkra, Techire, Akwatiakwaso, Fufuo ne Hohoe mu nyaa afebɔɔ ne animanim yi ara nnwuma (permanent and casual jobs) yɛeɛ.
english: In Government through the National Alternative Employment and Livelihood Programme (NAELP); reclaimed and reforested 645 hectares of degraded lands, and thus, creating over 2,300 direct jobs; and nursed 20 million economic seedlings to support the plantation development programme, creating 80,071 permanent and casual jobs for the youth in Akotom, Adinkra, Techire, Akwatiakwaso, Fufuo and Hohoe.

twi: Afe 2023 mu nso, Aban bɛkɔ so ayɛ deɛ ɛdidi soɔ yi: Bɛduadua nnua nam so asiesie asase hekta dodoɔ apem (1000) a asɛe wɔ mpɔtam pɔtee ahodoɔ bi mu, atintim nnua a wɔtumi nya mu sika sɛ ebia kube, abɛ, sitrɔs (ankaa) ne amango dodoɔ ɔpepem de aboa ama afuoyɛ mpontuo (plantation development) akɔ nkan asane de asi nnua dodoɔ a wɔatwitwa anan mu; Bɛbuebue beaeɛ ahodoɔ edu a wɔtintim nnua nketewa nam so ama nnipa dodoɔ mpem ɔha anya nnwuma ayɛ; na afei Yɛbɛma wɔn a wɔyɛ galamsey seesei ne wɔn a wɔnya bi a wɔbɛyɛ dodoɔ mpem aduonu (20,000) ne fam agudeɛtuo adwuma nketewa dodoɔ ahanu (200 small-scale mining companies) nteteeɛ afa fagudeɛtuo ho apɔmuden ho (mine health), ahobanbɔ nhyehyɛeɛ (safety standard) ne ɛkwan
english: In 2023, Government will continue to: Reclaim and stabilise 1000 hectares of degraded lands in selected communities, nurse 1 million economic trees such as coconut, oil palm, citrus and mango to support plantation development and re-afforestation; Establish at designated locations 10 seedlings nursery centres thus, creating 100,000 direct jobs; and train 20,000 illegal miners and potential illegal miners, 200 small-scale mining companies in mine health, safety

twi: 29 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ foforɔ ne ɛkwan pa a wɔtumi fa so yɛ fagudeɛtuo dwumadie mu ho.
english: Addition” 17 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget standard and the use of alternative safer and sustainable methods of ore extraction in small scale mining.

twi: 30 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ Wo-deɛ-hyɛ-aseɛ Dwumadie (YouStart) 48. Ɛyɛ aban anisoadehunu sɛ afe 2022-2025 mu no ɔbɛfa “wodeɛ- hyɛ-aseɛ dwumadie” no so ama mmabunu bosea a nsiho biara nni ho, ama wɔde abuebue nnwuma dodoɔ ɔpepem baako (one million jobs).
english: YouStart 48. Government intends to create a minimum of one million jobs for the youth over the period 2022-2025 through the provision of soft loans for the setting-up of youth-led enterprises under the YouStart programme.

twi: Saa dwumadie yi a ɛwɔ hɔ mfeɛ mmiɛnsa ntam yi aboa nnwuma a mmabunu na wɔdi anim (wɔn a wɔnni mmoroo mfeɛ aduanan (40 years) ne Nnwuma Nketewa ne Adantam (Small Medium Enterprises ,SMEs) aduɔson ama wɔn nsa aka mmoa sɛ ebia dwumadie ho nimdeɛ (capacity building), adwadifoɔ ho akwannya (access to markets), adwuamayɛ ho mmara-so-die ne adwadeɛ mudie.Sika dodoɔ a yɛakyekyɛ wɔ dwumadie yi mu yɛ Ghana sidi ɔpepem baako, mpem aduɔkron nwɔtwe (GH¢1.98 million).
english: The 3-year programme which offers support to youth-led (below the age of 40 years) Small Medium Enterprises (SMEs) with services such as capacity building, access to markets, compliance and quality assurance support has been successfully piloted with 70 beneficiaries, with an amount of GH¢1.98 million disbursed.

twi: Aban ne Ɔman Ghana Sikakorabea Nyinaa Nkabom Ekuo (Ghana Association of Banks (GAB) ne Dwadie Banke ahodoɔ dubaako eleven (11) commercial banks) de nsa ahyɛ nteaseɛ apam ase fa wo-deɛ-hyɛ-aseɛ (Youstart) dwumadie no ho.
english: Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Ghana Association of Banks (GAB) and eleven (11) commercial banks for implementation of the YouStart commercial programme.

twi: Ɛnam yei so enti sikakorabea ahodoɔ dubaako de sika dodoɔ, Ghana sidi ɔpepempem baako, ɔpepem ɔha aduosia nkron (GH¢1.169 billion) a ɛgyina hɔ ma sika dodoɔ a wɔatwa ato hɔ ama dwumadie no mu ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduasa.
english: Consequently, the banks have committed a total of GH¢1.169 billion, which represents 30% of the funding portfolio, for the programme.

twi: 31 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ Ghana Nnuadua dwumadie a ɛbɛsi ewiem nsakraeɛ ho ɔhaw ano 51. Afe 2022 mu no, yɛgyinaa dwumadie a wɔato edin” Ghana Nnuadua Ɛda” no so kyekyɛɛ nnua nketewa dodoɔ ɔpepem aduonu nsia, mpem aduonum enum (26.55 million seedlings) na wɔatumi atintim emu dodoɔ ɔpepem aduonu ɛnan , mpem aduanan ɛnan (24.44 million).

english: In addition, 12.9 million seedlings, including ofram, emire, wawa, kokrodua, teak, cedrela, gmelina, cassia, eucalyptus and mahogany species were supplied and planted.

twi: Ghana Nnuadua Ɛda (Green Ghana Day) 52. Yɛgyinaa Ɔman Nnuadua Dwumadie no so duaa nnua hɛkta dodoɔ mpem dubaako ne ahansia aduokron mmienu (11,692ha) a annuru hɛkta mpem dunson (17,000ha) a yɛyɛɛ adwene sɛ anka yɛbɛdua no.
english: Green Ghana Day 52. A total area of 11,692ha forest plantation was established against a revised target of 17,000ha under the National Afforestation Programme.

twi: Ɛsiane nsunsuansoɔ bɔne a Ewiem “ɔhyewdenden” (Global warming) de ba apɔmuden, nnuane ne Aman ahodoɔ a saa ɔhyew no ano yɛ den wɔ so dada sɛ ebia Ghana no sikasɛm mpontuo so no ama ɔhaw kɛseɛ abɛtɔ ewiase sikasɛm so.
english: Global warming poses major threats to the world economy given its negative impacts on health, food and directly to the economies of climate vulnerable countries like Ghana.

twi: Amaneɛbɔ bi a atɔ edwa wɔ deɛ wɔato edin sɛ V20 Adehwere ne Ɔsɛeɛ ho amaneɛbɔ 32 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ (“V20 Loss and Damage Report) no mu kyerɛ sɛ ɛfiri afe 2000 kɔsi 2019 mu no, ɛsiane ewiem nsakraeɛ ho nsunsuansoɔ enti, Ghanaman nko ara hweree dɔla ɔpepepem dunum, ɔpepem ahanu ne baako, ahansia aduɔkron enum ($15,200,001,695).
english: According to the V20 Loss and Damage Report, Ghana alone lost $15,200,001,695 from 2000 to 2019 to climate change.

english: Government will continue to pursue the development of droughttolerant crop varieties as an important climate adaptation measure and invest in irrigation infrastructure across the country

In line with Government’s commitment to ensuring that adequate logistics are available for effective and efficient administration of schools and educational directorates, Government procured and distributed 175 (66-seater) Buses, 71 Pick-Ups and 2 Tractors to Senior High Schools and Technical and Vocational Education and Training Institutes across the country.

twi: Afe 2022 mu no, Aban faa Mpɔtam Mpontuo ne Nsaanodwumasua sukuu ahodoɔ aduonu nkron so ( 29 Community Development and Vocational Technical Institutes) tetee mmarima mpem mmiɛnsa ahanson ne aduonu ɛnan (3,724) ne mmaa mpem mmiɛnsa ahanson ne dunum (3,715) wɔ nsaanodwuma mu sɛdeɛ wɔn nimdeɛ bɛkɔ nkan ama wɔanya nnwuma ayɛ anaa abuebue wɔn ara wɔn nnwuma afa so abrɛ ohia ase.
english: In 2022, Government trained 3,724 male and 3,715 female artisans in 29 Community Development and Vocational Technical Institutes to sharpen their technical and vocational skills for employment and job creation opportunities as well as reduce poverty.

twi: Bio, yɛtetee mpɔtam adekyerɛfoɔ dodoɔ ahanu aduanan nwɔtwe (248 community educators) wɔ mpɔtam mpontuo ne Asetena mu banbɔ ho nimdeɛ mu wɔ Kwaso Mpɔtam Mpontuo kɔlegyi hɔ sɛdeɛ wɔbɛnya nimdeɛ de aboaboa mpɔtamfoɔ ano ama wɔatu mpontuo ho anammɔn.
english: Additionally, 248 community educators were trained in community development and social protection at the Rural Development College in Kwaso to help mobilize communities for development activities.

twi: Afe 2023 mu no, Aban bɛtete Mpɔtam Adekyerɛfoɔ dodoɔ ahanum wɔ Asetenam Banbɔ ne Mpɔtam Mpontuo ho (500 Community Educators in Social Protection and Community Development) asane ahyehyɛ nteteeɛ foforɔ koraa afa nimdeɛ a ɛma adwumanya ɛkwan bue a ɛnyɛ afuoyɛ ho sɛ ebia saminayɛ, anaa kentenwono ne aboa nwoma ho
english: Government in 2023 will train 500 Community Educators in Social Protection and Community Development and develop new training modules on non-farm job opportunities such as soap making, kente weaving and leather works to promote local economic development and income generation.

twi: Apɔmuden 68. Atiridii yadeɛ gu so ka yadeɛ edu a ɛkum nnipa pa ara wɔ Ghana no ho.
english: Health 68. Malaria continues to be amongst the top ten killer diseases in Ghana.

twi: Yei enti sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na Aban bɛtu atiridii yadeɛ ase no, ɔde afidie bi a wɔfrɛ no “LSM Implement app” a ɛtumi kyerɛ baabi a ntontom dɔre ma wɔhye wɔn ase wɔ Mansini ahodoɔ mu aba.
english: Thus, as part of Government’s efforts to eliminate malaria, an application (LSM Implement app) for mapping and treatment of mosquito breeding sites in the districts has been rolled out.

twi: Ho Nteteeɛ Ayaresabea no (Ho Teaching Hospital) nso de afidie bi a wɔfrɛ no CT-Scan ne deɛ wɔfrɛ no “endoscopy” a ɛtumi hwehwɛ nnipadua mu nyinaa aba, asane de ɛhyɛn a wɔtumi de di akɔneaba kɔsa yareɛ (mobile clinic van) aba de kyinkyini kokɔ mmeaɛmmeaɛ de boa ayaresa.
english: The Ho Teaching Hospital introduced CT-Scan and endoscopy services and acquired a mobile clinic van to support outreach services.

twi: Afe 2022 mu no, Aban wiee dwumadie ahodoɔ a ɛdidi soɔ yi: Mpɔtam ayaresabea ahodoɔ a ɛwowɔ (CHPS compounds) Debiso, Nsutam, ne Tiawia; Mansini ayaresabea wɔ Konongo; Ayaresa ne ahomegyeɛ beaeɛ (treatment and holding centres) wɔ Aflao, Elubo, Keta, Kumasi Anafoɔ, ne Sewua; ne ahododoɔ Beaeɛ (Fevers Unit) ne COVID-19 ɔhwɛ beaeɛ (Isolation Centre) wɔ Korle Bu.
english: In 2022, Government completed the following projects: construction of CHPS compounds at Debiso, Nsutam, and Tiawia; a district hospital at Konongo; treatment and holding centres at Addition” 24 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget Aflao, Elubo, Keta, Kumasi South, and Sewua; and Fevers Unit and COVID-19 Isolation Centre at Korle Bu.

twi: Afe 2023 mu no, aban bɛkɔ so ayɛ apɔmuden adwumayɛfoɔ a yɛde wɔn kɔ amannɔne no ho nhyehyɛeɛ pa nam so awie nteaseɛ Apam a ɔne Nyiresi Aban (United Kingdom) reyɛ afa wɔn ho no.
english: In 2023, Government will continue to regularise the exportation of health professionals by concluding on the Memorandum of Understanding between the Governments of Ghana and the United Kingdom.

twi: Aban bɛtoa adwuma a ɔredi fa Ɔman Paneɛwɔ Adwumakuo (National Vaccine Institute) ne Ghana Adwumakuo a ɛbrɛ Nyarewa ase (National Vaccine Institute and Ghana) no so .Bio afe 2023 mu no, ɔbɛhwɛ de atiridii mpaneɛ ho aduro aba nam so abrɛ owuo dodoɔ ano ase wɔ Ɔman yi mu.
english: Government will continue with the establishment of the National Vaccine Institute and Ghana Centre for Disease Control. Additionally, malaria vaccines will be introduced in 2023 to reduce high mortality rate in the country.

english: Human Security 72. Government in 2022 recruited 5,000 personnel into the Ghana Police Service as part of its drive to improve manpower of security personnel and contribute towards the maintenance of law and order.

twi: Polisi Adwumakuo no tee deɛ yɛfrɛ no Nsɛm A ano yɛ den Nkorabata” (“Cold Cases Unit”) wɔ Awurakasɛm Nhwehwɛmu Adwumam (Criminal Investigations Department) (CID) hɔ, maa polisifoɔ a wɔtumi ko tia korɔnobɔ a etuo da so dii dwuma (Anti- Armed Robbery Taskforce) (AATF), tee ɔfa bi a emu polisifoɔ de moto kɔ aporɔ wɔ nkuro akɛseɛ pɔtee bi mu, (Motorbike Patrol Unit), wɔhyɛɛ adwuma no fa bi a ɛkɔ aporɔbɔ (Police Mounted Squadron and a Canine (K-9) no ase.
english: The Service established the Cold Cases Unit at the Criminal Investigations Department (CID), deployed specialised Anti- Armed Robbery Taskforce (AATF), created a Motorbike Patrol Unit in selected major cities, introduced a Police Mounted Squadron and a Canine (K-9) unit for patrols.

twi: Mmara a wɔde tee polisi adwuma no ma ho ɛkwan ma wɔyɛ saa nhyehyɛeɛ pa ahodoɔ yi nyinaa nam so ma banbɔ di mu. english: These innovations are in line with their mandate to promote internal security in the country. 74. Government continued works on Phase III of the Security Services Housing Programme which comprises the construction of 320 units for the Ghana Police Service at the Ghana National Police Training School, Tesano.

english: Government through National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) supported 15,772 disaster victims.

In 2023, the Police Service will undertake the following: establish Formed Police Unit (FPUs) in 16 police regions to ensure effective and efficient public order and crowd control; re-train and retool the existing Crime Combat and Action Units to be proactive in fighting violent crime such as armed robbery; deploy 1,500 men with 100 vehicles to increase patrol duties in the communities and on the highways to curb the rising spate of armed robbery; and expand Traffic Surveillance Centres to all the 18 Police Regions to ensure efficient and effective traffic management to reduce indiscipline and carnage on our roads.

twi: Aban bɛtoa Ɔman nkyerɛkyerɛ Dwumadie a ɛfa sɛdeɛ wɔbrɛ atoyerɛnkyɛm ano ase no so, ayere dawurobɔ dwumadie a ɛfa asasewosoɔ ho no mu, ayɛ nhyehyɛeɛ a ɛnam so bɛbɔ amaneɛ ntɛm so afa nsuyire ho wɔ amantam ne mansini bi mu ho, sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a atoyerɛnkyɛm rebɛsi a wɔbɛhunu no ntɛm so.
english: Government will also continue public education campaigns on disaster risk reduction, intensify sensitization programmes on earthquake, strengthen community resilience for early warning by setting up flood information system in selected regions and districts.

twi: Banbɔ Adwumayɛfoɔ Adansie Dwumadie (Phase IV of the Security Services Housing Programme) no fa a ɛtɔ so ɛnan no bɛfiri aseɛ ama Ghana Afiase Adwumakuo (Ghana Prisons Service.) no wɔ afe 2023 mu.
english: Work on the Phase IV of the Security Services Housing Programme will commence in 2023 for the Ghana Prisons Service.

Aban bɛfa Nsrahwɛ Adwumakuo (Ghana Tourism Authority) (GTA) no so, agyina nhyehyɛeɛ a wɔato edin hunu Ghana (See Ghana), di Ghana aduane (Eat Ghana), Hyɛ Ghana (Wear Ghana atadeɛ) ne Nya atenka ma Ghana (Feel Ghana’) nhyehyɛeɛ no so ahyehyɛ dawubɔ dwumadie nam so ahyɛ nkuran afa hia a ɛhia sɛ yɛtɔ Ghana nneɛma ho.
english: Tourism 79. Government under the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) will mount an aggressive awareness programme under its ‘See Ghana, Eat Ghana, Wear Ghana and Feel Ghana’ campaign to encourage patronage of made in Ghana products in the tourism and hospitality industry.

twi: Aban ne ahɔhogyebea wuranom ne aduanenoafoɔ bɛdi nsawɔsoɔ ama wɔatɔn ɔman yi mu nnuane ne anonneɛ, de ɔman mu adwinneɛ, nkonnwa ne ahyehyɛdeɛ asiesie atenaeɛ a wɔdi dwuma hɔ no sɛdeɛ ɛbɛte nneɛma a wɔkra firi amannɔne wɔ wɔn dwumadie no mu. english: Government will engage with hoteliers and restauranteurs to serve local food and beverages, use local artefacts, furniture and fixtures, in the interior decoration of hospitality outlets in order to reduce the import component of inputs for the operation of businesses in the sector.

english: Addition” 26 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget 81. In line with Government’s policy to promote investments and private sector participation in the development of tourist attraction sites, the GTA will work closely with Ghana Investment Promotion Centre (GIPC) to provide incentive packages for local and foreign investors.

twi: Adwadeɛ a Yɛde Kɔ Amannɔne ho Anammɔntuo 82. Nnansa yi mu no, amannɔne nneɛma dodoɔ a tɛkra ba ɔman yi mu no yi mu no ama Ghana sidi no mu duru akɔ fam ama sikasɛm ama amannɔne edwadie nnyinasoɔ gyinapɛn ayɛ basaa.
english: Export Drive 82. In recent times, Ghana’s heavy dependence on imports has placed a heavy pressure on the Cedi thus creating an unfavourable balance of payments position

twi: Ghana covid 19 Asetɔre ne Ankorankorɛ Nnwuma mu Nkanyan ho mmoa dwumadie no fa a ɛtɔ so mmienu (Phase 2 of Ghana CARES) mu no, Aban bɛboa ankorankorɛ nnwuma a wɔwɔ mmeaeɛ pɔtee bi ama wɔayɛ adwadeɛ a ɛbɛtumi ahyɛ deɛ wɔkra no anan, apagya nneɛma a yɛde kɔ amannɔne kɔtɔn mu, ayɛ nhyehyɛeɛ a ɛbɛboa nnwuma ama wɔatumi ayɛ saa adwadeɛ ahodoɔ no.
english: Under Phase 2 of Ghana CARES, Government will provide support to the private sector in targeted sectors to accelerate competitive import substitution and export expansion and an enabling environment to support businesses to engage in the production of these products.

twi: Yei enti, Aban bɛyɛ nhyehyɛeɛ nam so ne nnwuma ahodoɔ a ɛwɔ hɔ dada ne deɛ afei na wɔrebɛfiri aseɛ aka wɔn ho abom nam so atrɛ nnwuma no mu, ɔbɛsiesie, asane de mfidie a ɛbɛyɛ adwadeɛ pɔtee a yɛde ani asi so no adi dwuma.
english: Further to this, Government will promote the formation of partnerships with existing and prospective businesses to expand, rehabilitate and establish manufacturing plants targeted at these selected items.

twi: Mmaa Ne Mmarima, Mmɔfra Ne Asetenam Banbɔ 84. Afe 2022 mu, Aban nam “sukuu mu adidie kwa” (Ghana School Feeding Programme (GSFP) nhyehyɛeɛ so maa mmɔfra dodoɔ Ɔpepepem mmiɛnsa, mpem ahansia aduonu, ahanan aduosia nwɔtwe (3,620,468 pupils) a na wɔwɔ aban sukuu mpem edu ahanwɔtwe aduasa mmienu mu (10,832 public basic schools)
english: Gender, Children and Social Protection 84. In 2022, Government through the Ghana School Feeding Programme (GSFP) fed 3,620,468 pupils in 10,832 public basic schools with one hot, nutritious meal for every school-going day.

twi: Ɛnam yei so maa mmɔfra dodoɔ a wɔkɔ sukuu a wɔwɔ (mmɔtafowa sukuu) KG, Mfitiaseɛ (Primary) ne Adantam (JHS) gyinapɛn no kɔɔ soro wɔ afe 2020/21 sukuu afe no mu. Mmɔtafowa sukuu kɔɔ soro ɔha mu nkyɛmu ɔha ne dunwɔtwe (118%), Mfitiaseɛ kɔduru ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduanan (40%) ɛnna Adantam Sukuu kɔduruu ɔha mu nkyɛmu aduɔson mmienu (72%).
english: This has resulted in a cumulative increase in enrolment as at 2020/21 academic year, for KG, Primary and JHS has been 118%, 40% and 72% respectively.

twi: Aban faa aduanenoafoɔ (caterers) ne aduanenoa aboafoɔ (cooks) mmaa mpem aduasa mmienu, ahanan aduɔkron nsia (32,496 caterers and cooks) sɛdeɛ wɔn sikasɛm bɛyɛ yie ama wɔatumi ahwɛ wɔn abusua.
english: Addition” 27 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget 85. Government employed 32,496 caterers and cooks especially women, to improve their income level to take care of their families.

twi: Bio Aban buee mfudeɛtɔ ho akwannya maa akuafoɔ nam so maa wɔn sikasɛm nyaa nnyinasoɔ.
english: Government further created a ready market for local farmers thereby boosting the local economy.

twi: Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na botaeɛ a ɛne sɛ yɛbɛma onibiefoɔ aduane a nnuanennuro ahyɛ mu ma enti no, Aban tuaa Asetena mu Nkuranhyɛ a ɛko Ɛtia Ohia (Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) ho sika no mmɔho enum maa fidua ahodoɔ mpem mmiɛnsa aduanan ɛnan, ahasa aduɔwɔtwe nkron (344,389).
english: To achieve the objective of smoothening the daily consumption and nutritional level of extremely poor households, Government paid five cycles of Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) cash grants to 344,389 households.

twi: Afe 2023 mu no, Aban bɛkɔ so ama adesuafoɔ aduane pa a nnuanennuro ahyɛ mu ma sukuu da biara.
english: In 2023, Government will continue to provide one hot, nutritious meal to school pupils on each school-going day.

twi: Aban paa Nnipatɔn Adwumakuo (Trafficking (HT) ne Ahohiahia Tebea ho ɔhwɛ (Trauma-Informed Care Center) Adwumam ho ntoma nam so maa mmɔfra aduonu ɛnan, mmaa mpanimfoɔ aduanan nsia ne mmarima mpanimfoɔ aduonu nson a na wɔatɔn wɔn na wɔakɔ ahohiahia tebea no mu no ayarehwɛ.
english: Government commissioned the Human Trafficking (HT) secretariat and Trauma-Informed Care Center and provided comprehensive trauma-informed care to 24 child, 46 adult female, and 27 adult male victims of human trafficking.

twi: Aban bɛkɔ so de ahohiahia ho ɔhwɛ a ɛfata ama wɔn a wɔbɛnya wɔn tiri adidi mu wɔ Nnipatɔn mu no, na wayɛ nhyehyɛeɛ ako atia nnipatɔn, mpɔtam nsawɔsodie na wasane ahyehyɛ dwumadie a wɔnam so bɛtwe nnwumakuo a wɔko tia nnipatɔn no adwene asi nnipatɔn ho ɔhaw so.
english: Government will continue to provide comprehensive trauma care to survivors of Human Trafficking and undertake preventive mechanisms against trafficking in persons, community dialogues as well as embark on awareness raising programs to sensitise stakeholders on issues of human trafficking

twi: 42 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ AWIEEƐ 90. Afe 2023 mu no, Aban bɛkɔ so aboa Asetenam Aboadeɛ ho Nnwuma ahodoɔ no, ahwɛ ama mpontunnwuma, kuayɛ, mfidinnwuma ne nsanodwumayɛ akɔ nkan.
english: Addition” 28 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget CONCLUSION 90. In 2023, Government will continue to support the services sector, Infrastructural Development, Agriculture, Industry, and Entrepreneurship.

twi: Yei enti, yɛsrɛ sɛ Ɔman mma nyinaa mfa wɔn ho nnye ɔman kyekyere nhyehyɛeɛ yi mu bi wɔ ɛberɛ a yɛretu anammɔn yi sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a yɛn nyinaa bɛbom atwa yɛn brɛ so aba adi.
english: We therefore call upon citizen’s to be actively involved in the nation building agenda as we put our hands to the plough, so that we can happily reap the rewards of our collective toils.

twi: Onyankopɔn nhyira Ɔman Ghana!!!
english: God Bless Our Homeland Ghana!!!

twi: 43 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ NSƐMFUA ASEKYERƐ (SIKASƐM NHYEHYƐEƐ MU NSƐMFUA) Mansini Baako Afididwuma Baako (1D1F): Yei yɛ mfidinnwuma ahodoɔ a yɛbɛbuebue wɔ mansini mu na ɛnam so ama mfidinnwuma atu mpɔn wɔ Ghana.
english: Addition” 29 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget GLOSSARY (BUDGET TERMINOLOGY) 1D1F (One District, One Factory): The setting up of factories and industries which, will in turn, move the country towards greater industrialization.

twi: Yei botaeɛ ne sɛ nnwuma bɛbu so wɔ ɔman yi mu na Ghanafoɔ a wɔwɔ ɔman yi afanan nyinaa anya adwuma ayɛ.
english: It is aimed at creating more jobs for Ghanaians across the length and breadth of the country.

twi: Abibirem Aman mu Edwadie A Akwansideɛ Nni ho (African Continental Free Trade Area – AfCFTA): Yei yɛ edwa kɛseɛ a wɔahyehyɛ ama Abibirem Adwdeɛyɛ Nnwumakuo a ɛbɛboa ama wɔde wɔn adwadeɛ akɔ Abibirem aman so akɔtɔn a wɔrentua edwadie mu ɛtoɔ ahodoɔ biara na wɔanya edwa kɛseɛ a ɛwɔ Abibirem ha no ho mfasoɔ.
english: African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA): A market created to eliminate tariffs on intra-Africa trade, making it easier for African businesses to trade within the continent and benefit from the growing African market.

twi: Ɔhaw-anosie (Alleviation): Yei yɛ ɛkwan wɔfa so ma ɔhaw bi ho nsunsuansoɔ ano brɛ ase.
english: Alleviation: This is the process of making a problem less severe.

twi: Sika Mu Nkyekyɛmu (Allocation): Yei yɛ ɛkwan a wɔfa so kyekyɛ ɔman sika mu ma Aban asoɛeɛ ahodoɔ no ne nnwumakuo ahodoɔ no ma wɔde di dwuma ma ɔmanfoɔ.
english: Allocation: The process of sharing or distributing resources amoung government agencies and departments.

twi: Afadeɛ (Apparel): Afadeɛ anaa atadeɛ pɔtee bi a wɔtɔn wɔ sotɔɔ mu. Amannɔne Edwadie ho Gyinapin (Balance of Payments): Yei yɛ edwadie a ɛkɔ so wɔ ɔman bi ne ewiase aman afoforɔ ntam wɔ ɛberɛ pɔtee bi mu sɛ ebia, abosome mmiɛnsa biara wɔ afe no mu anaa mpo afe no nyinaa mu no ho anodisɛm anaa nkontabuo.
english: Ancilliary: Additional or providing additional support or help Apparel: Clothes of a particular type when they are being sold in a shop Balance of Payments: Is a statement of all transactions made between entities in one country and the rest of the world over a defined period, such as a quarter or a year.

twi: Sikasɛm Nhyehyɛeɛ (Budget): Sikasɛm nhyehyɛeɛ gyina hɔ ma nhyehyɛeɛ a Aban ayɛ afa ɛkwan a ɔbɛfa so anya sika ne deɛ ɔde saa sika no bɛyɛ ho.
english: Budget: A budget is a plan that outlines where to get money from and what to spend it on.

twi: Nhwɛsoɔ ne sɛ, abusua bi bɛtumi ayɛ sikasɛm nhyehyɛeɛ nam so akyerɛ sika dodoɔ a wɔwɔ ne nneɛma ahodoɔ a ɛhia sɛ wɔde sika no yɛ no nnidisoɔ nnidisoɔ.
english: For instance, a family can draw up a budget that will show how much money is available and how it should be prioritised for spending (for example, rent, utilities and food).

twi: Ɛbɛtumi ayɛ ɛdan ho ɛka, nsuo ne nkanea ɛka ɛnna aduane ho ɛka) Ɛkɔba sɛ wɔhia sika no dodoɔ a, ɛho bɛhia sɛ abusua no bɛhwehwɛ sika no bi aka ho anaa mpo wɔbɛkɔ akɔbɔ bosea.
english: If more money is needed, the family would need to consider raising more income or taking a loan.

twi: Asɛ Ɔkraman (Canine): Deɛ ɛfa ɔkraman ho anaa ɛsɛ ɔkraman.
english: Budget Deficit: Occurs when expenditures exceed revenue Canine: Relating to or resembling a dog or dogs.

twi: Mpontunnwuma ho Sika (Capital Expenditure): Yei yɛ sika a yɛde yɛ mpontunnwuma sɛ ebia akwanyie, sukuudansie, ayaresabea dansie, atwene-sie, akwantusɛm, nsuo, mfidie akɛseɛ ne deɛ ɛkeka ho. Abɔnta Lɔre Ɛkwan (Carriageway): Ɛyɛ lɔre ɛkwan no ɔfa a ahyɛn tumi fa so.
english: Capital Expenditure: This is money spent on major infrastructure projects such as roads, schools, hospitals, bridges, transport, water systems, plant and machinery etc. Carriageway: It is the part of a road used by vehicular traffic.

twi: Adwumayɛfoɔ akatua (Compensation of Employees): Yei yɛ adwumayɛfoɔ bosome akatua, Sika ahodoɔ, asetenam ahotosoɔ sika, akwankɔgya sika ne deɛ ɛkeka ho a wɔtua ma Aban adwumayɛfoɔ.
english: Compensation of Employees: This is made up of salaries and salaryrelated allowances such as social security, gratuities and pensions paid to public sector workers.

twi: Onipadua mu nhwehwɛmu (Endoscopy): IYei yɛ nhwehwɛmu bi a wɔyɛ wɔ onipadua no mu.
english: Endoscopy: It is a test to look inside your body

twi: Ɛka ne Ɔman mu Adwadeɛ Nyinaa Ntam Ntotoho (Debt-to-GDP ratio): Yei yɛ sikassɛm mu gyinaberɛ a ɛda adi wɔ ɛberɛ a yɛde ɔman bi ɛka a ɔde no atoto ɔman no mu adwadeɛ nyinaa bo a ɛsom no ho na yɛahunu sɛdeɛ ɔman no gyinaberɛ no teɛ.
english: Addition” 30 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget Debt-to-GDP ratio: It is the ratio of a country's public debt to its gross domestic product.

twi: Biribi bo a ɛsom so-teɛ (Depreciation): Yei yɛ sɛdeɛ agyapadeɛ bi bo a ɛsom no so teɛ wɔ ɛberɛ pɔtee bi mu anaa sɛ sɛdeɛ sɛ wode ɔman bi sika toto aman afoforɔ deɛ ho a, emu duru no wɔ fam. Mpontuo mu Aboafoɔ (Development Partners): Yei gyina hɔ ma Aman anaa nnwumakuo a wɔboa Aman a afei na wɔretu mpɔn ma wɔduru wɔn mpontuo botaeɛ ho.
english: Depreciation: It is a reduction in the value of an asset over time or a decrease in the value of a currency relative to other currencies Development Partners (DPs): This refers to countries and/or organizations that collaborate with developing countries to achieve their developmental goals.

twi: Yei bɛtumi ayɛ akuhodoɔ bi te sɛ Amansan Fotoɔ Adwumakuo (lnternational Monetary Fund- IMF),Ewiase Sikakorabea (World Bank), Abibirem Mpontuo Sikakorabea (African Development Bank) ne deɛ ɛkeka ho. !tumi nso yɛ ankorankorɛ aman bi te sɛ Germany, Nyiresi Aburokyire, Amɛrika, ne wɔn a wɔkeka ho.
english: DPs can be multilateral, e.g. International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Bank, African Development Bank (AfDB) or bilateral which consists of individual countries like Germany, United Kingdom and the United States of America (USA).

twi: 45 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ Afe Awieeɛ Nneɛma Boɔ-Sorokɔ (End Year Inflation): Yei yɛ mpɛmpɛnsoɔ a nneɛma boɔ kɔduru wɔ $pɛnimma bosome mu wɔ afe pɔtee bi mu.
english: End Year Inflation: The level of inflation experienced in December of a year in consideration.

twi: Dwumadie ho sika a yɛadi aboro so (Expenditure Overrun): Yei si wɔ ɛberɛ a, sika a yɛde adi dwuma ahodoɔ no aboro deɛ yɛtwa too hɔ wɔ sikasɛm nhyehyɛeɛ mu a mmarahyɛbadwa gye too mu no so.
english: Expenditure Overrun: This occurs when Government spending exceeds the Budget amount approved by Parliament.

twi: Amannɔne Edwadie Sikakorabea (EXIM - Export-Import) Bank: Ghana Amannɔne Edwadie Sikakorabea (Export-Import Bank - GEXIM) yɛ sikakorabea bi a wɔnam mmara a ɛtɔ so ahankron ne dubaako (Ghana Export-Import Bank Act 2016 - Act 911) so buee wɔ ɔman yi mu wɔ afe 2016 mu a, ɛbɛboa aban wɔ adwadeɛ a yɛde kɔ amannɔne kɔtɔn ho edwadie no ama ase atim.
english: EXIM (Export-Import) Bank: Ghana Export-Import Bank (GEXIM) was established by the Ghana Export-Import Bank Act 2016 (Act 911) to support the government of Ghana’s quest for a feasible and sustainable export led economy.

twi: Adwadeɛ A Yɛde Kɔ Amannɔne ho Edwadie Asoɛeɛ Ahodoɔ (Export Trade Houses -ETH): Yeinom yɛ edwadie ho nnwuma bi a wɔboa nnwumakuo a wɔhia mmoa ne nimdeɛ wɔ amannɔne edwadie mu fa sɛdeɛ wɔn nsa bɛka adwadeɛ bi afiri amannɔne anaa wɔde adwadeɛ bi bɛkɔ amannɔne.
english: Export Trade Houses (ETH): They are trading houses that provide a service for businesses that want international trade experts to receive or deliver goods or services.

twi: Sikasɛm mu Sintɔ (Fiscal Deficit): Yei yɛ nnyinasoɔ a wɔhwɛ ho ansa na ɔman bi anya ɛkwan abɔ bosea de adi dwuma a bosea ho nsiho-tua ka ho bie. Sikasɛm ho Anammɔntuo Ahodoɔ (Fiscal Operations): Yeinom yɛ sikasɛm ho akontabuo ne amaneɛbɔ, sika ho ntotoeɛ, dwetire ho dwumadie, sikatua, akatua ho nsɛm, agyapadeɛ, dwumadie so-hwɛ ne ɛkatua.
english: Fiscal Deficit: It reflects the borrowing requirements of the government for financing the expenditure inclusive of interest payments Fiscal Operations: They are accounting and financial reporting, cash management, investments, accounts payable, payroll, fixed assets, internal control, and debt service management Fiscal Policy: It refers to the use of government spending and tax policies to influence economic conditions, especially macroeconomic conditions.

twi: Sikasɛm ho Mmara (Fiscal Policy): Yei yɛ ɛkwan a aban fa so de sika di dwuma ne ɛtoɔ ho nhyehyɛeɛ ahodoɔ a ɛboa ma sikasɛm mu mpontuo nnyinasoɔ anaa nneɛma a ɛma ɔman sikasɛm gyina yie no ase tim.
english: Fiscal Stress: It is a concept that seeks to measure the extent to which a local government is in danger of a fiscal crisis warranting intercession by the State, especially actions that could reduce local control.

twi: Fa-me-kwa Ntoasoɔ Sukuukorɔ (FREE SHS): Fa-me-kwa Ntoasoɔ Sukuukorɔ yi yɛ Aban nhyehyɛeɛ foforɔ a Ɔmanpanin Nana Akuffo-Addo aban de puee edwa wɔ Ɛbɔ bosome mu wɔ afe 2017 mu sɛ JHS osukuuni biara a ɔbɛbɔ ne ho mmɔden wɔ sɔhwɛ mu no, ɔbɛnya ɛkwan wɔ Ntoasoɔ Sukuu mu akɔsua adeɛ a ɔrentua hwee.
english: FREE SHS: The Free SHS (Free Senior High School) policy is a Government of Ghana initiative introduced by the President Nana Akuffo-Addo administration in September 2017 that guarantees free access to SHS education for any accademically qualified JHS student

twi: Ghana Ɔhwɛpa Dwumadie (Ghana Cares): Dwumadie yi wɔ nhyehyɛeɛ mmienu a ɛyɛ anammɔn ahodoɔ a Aban adi kan atu wɔ Coronavirus Nsunsuansoɔ Anosie Dwumadie ho no ntoasoɔ.
english: Addition” 31 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget Ghana Cares: It is a two-phase programme that builds on the immediate actions already taken by Government under the Coronavirus Alleviation Programme (CAP).

twi: Sika a yɛde kyɛ Aban (Grants): Yeinom yɛ sika ho mmoa ahodoɔ a Mpontuo mu Aboafoɔ de boa Aban a ɛnyɛ adeɛ a Aban bɛtua.
english: Grants: These are types of financial assistance given to Government by development partners and for which Government does not have to be pay back.

twi: Sika a wɔtua ma Aban Nnwuma ahodoɔ (Grants to other Government Units): Yei gyina hɔ ma sika a, mmara hyɛ sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ wɔtua kɔgu Mansini Mmarahyɛbadwa Fotoɔ “DACF” no mu, Lɔrekwan Fotoɔ “Road Fund” mu, Nwomasua Fotoɔ “GETFUND” mu, Fango ho Dwumadie Fotoɔ “Petroleum Related Fund” ne Ɔman Apɔmuden ho Fotoɔ “National Health Fund” mu.
english: Grants to other Government Units: These constitute payments that are required by law such as District Assemblies’ Common Fund (DACF), Road Fund, Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFUND), Petroleum Related Fund and National Health Fund.

twi: Ɔman mu Adwadeɛ Nyinaa Bo A Ɛsom (Gross Domestic Product (GDP): Yei kyerɛ nneɛma a yɛyɛ wɔ ɔman yi mu wɔ ɛberɛ pɔtee bi mu no nyinaa bo a ɛsom.
english: Gross Domestic Product (GDP): This refers to the total value of all final demand goods and services produced in the country over a specific time.

twi: Amannɔne Sika dodoɔ A Ɔman Wɔ (Gross International Reserves):Yei yɛ susudua a yɛfa so hunu sɛdeɛ ɔman bi sikasɛm ahoɔden a ɔwɔ sɛ ɔbɛtumi atɔ nneɛma afiri amannɔne no teɛ wɔ ɛberɛ pɔtee bi mu. Yei boa ma yɛde ɔman bi fotoɔ toto ɔman foforɔ bi deɛ ho a yɛhunu sɛdeɛ ɔman no sikasɛm ahoɔden a ɔwɔ no teɛ.
english: Gross International Reserves: This measures a country’s foreign currency ability to buy goods and services from foreign countries over a period; it also supports the strength of the local currency in relation to currencies of other nations.

twi: 47 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ Edwa-so Nneɛma-boɔ-sorokɔ (Headline Inflation): Yei yɛ nneɛmaboɔ-sorokɔ ho amaneɛbɔ a ɛfiri Adetɔfoɔ Nsusuiɛ a ɛfa nneɛma boɔ ho a Adwumayɛfoɔ ho Nkontabuo Ɔfese (Bureau of Labor Statistics) de to edwa bosome biara.
english: Headline Inflation: It is the raw inflation figure reported through the Consumer Price Index (CPI) that is released monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).

twi: Ɔman Mu Adwadeɛyɛ (Import Substitution): Yei yɛ ɛkwan a yɛfa so yɛ adwadeɛ wɔ ɔman yi ara mu de hyɛ adwadeɛ ahodoɔ bi a yɛkra firi amannɔne no anan mu na mmom ɛnyɛ sɛ yɛbɛyɛ adwadeɛ de akɔ amannɔne akɔtɔn na ɛnam saa ɔman yi ara mu adwadeɛyɛ yi so ma ɔman yi mu mfidinnwuma tu mpɔn.
english: Import Substitution: A strategy that emphasizes the replacement of imports with domestically produced goods, rather than the production of goods for export to encourage the development of domestic industry Inflation: The rate of increase in general price level of goods and services over a period.

twi: Nneɛma boɔ-sorokɔ (Inflation): Yei gyina hɔ ma sɛdeɛ dwumadie ahodoɔ ne adwadeɛ boɔ si kɔ soro wɔ ɛberɛ pɔtee bi mu.
english: Import substitution: A strategy that emphasizes the replacement of imports with domestically produced goods, rather than the production of goods for export to encourage the development of domestic industry Inflation: The rate of increase in general price level of goods and services over a period.

twi: Nsiho ho Ɛka (Interest cost): Yei yɛ bosea ho nsiho dodoɔ a ɛsɛ sɛ ɔkafoɔ tua wɔ bosea a wabɔ ho anaa biribi a ɔde ho ɛka wɔ ɛberɛ a ɔntuaa sika botene no ankasa nwieeɛ.
english: Interest cost: It refers to the cumulative amount of interest a borrower pays on a loan or other debt while it is outstanding.

twi: Nsiho-tua (Interest payments): Yei yɛ bosea anaa agyapadeɛ bi ho nsiho a ɔkafoɔ anaa deɛ wafiri agyapadeɛ no tua.
english: Interest payments: They are the cost of borrowing money or payment of interest on a loan or mortgage

twi: Yei ho nhwɛsoɔ ne sikasɛm mpontuo, nneɛmaboɔ sorokɔ, adwumayɛ mu mpontuo mpɛmpɛnsoɔ, ɔman yi ne aman afoforɔ ntam edwadie mu mmɔdemmɔ, sɛdeɛ aban no sikasɛm ntotoeɛ kankorɔ anaa sintɔ teɛ ɛne sɛdeɛ gyinaeɛ ahodoɔ a Ghana Sikakorabea Baatan bɛsie no bɛka nneɛma boɔ sorokɔ wɔ ɔman no mu. 48 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ Nteaseɛ Apam (Memorandum of Understanding - MoU): Ɛyɛ krataa so nnyetom a ɛfa gyinaeɛsie bi ho anammɔntuo bi ho a afanu anaa nnipa a wɔboro saa agye atom sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde di dwumat.
english: Addition” 32 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget IPEP (Infrastructure for Poverty Eradication Programme): The Infrastructure for Poverty Eradication Programme (IPEP) is one of the flagship programmes of the NPP Government that aims at eradicating poverty and minimalizing inequality, especially in the rural and deprived communities through the provision of basic infrastructure Macroeconomic targets: These are measurements used to access the performance of the economy.

twi: Nkorabata/Ɔfa (Module): Ɛyɛ biribi nkorabata a yɛtumi keka bom ma ɛyɛ adekorɔ no kɛseɛ. Sikasɛm ho Anammɔntuo Nhyehyɛeɛ (Monetary policy): Ɛyɛ nhyehyɛeɛ a ɔman sikasɛm so adwumakuo baatan no fa so toto boseabɔ ho nsiho wɔ ɛberɛ tiawa bi mu anaa sɛdeɛ ɔde sika foforɔ bɛpue edwa, nsiho dodoɔ nyinaa ho nsɛm sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a ɛbɛboa ama nneɛma boɔ agyina faako.
english: Examples include economic growth, inflation, changes in the level of employment, trade performance with other countries, relative success or failure of government economic policies and the decisions made by the Bank of Ghana which affects money demand and supply in the economy.

twi: Nnwuma Nketewa Mu Mpontuo Dwumadie - MSME (Micro And Small Buisness Developmet Programme): Nnwuma Nketewa yɛ ankorankorɛ nnwuma a wɔtumi fa nnipa kakra bi a dwetire a adwuma no gyina soɔ no mmoro sika dodoɔ pɔtee bi so.
english: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU): It is a formal agreement that outlines plans for a common line of action between two or more parties.

twi: Ɔman-kyekyere Atuhoakyɛfoɔ- NABCo (Nation Builders Corps): Yei yɛ adwene foforɔ koraa a Ghana Aban de puee edwa a ɔnam so bɛma mmeranteɛ ne mmabaawa a wɔawie asuapɔn no bɛnya adwuma ayɛ wɔ ankorankorɛ anaa Aban nnwuma mu na wɔaboa de wɔn nimdeɛ apɛ asetenam ɔhaw ahodoɔ nnannuaguberɛ, na yei aboa wɔn ma wɔanya osuahunu a ɛbɛboa Ɔman sikasɛm mpontuo.
english: Module: It is one of a set of separate parts that can be joined together to form a larger Monetary policy: It is the policy adopted by the monetary authority of a nation to control either the interest rate payable for very shortterm borrowing or the money supply, interest rate, to ensure price stability.

twi: Ɔman Adwumakuo A Ɛhwɛ Mfidinnwuma Nketwa So- (National Board for Small Scale Industries- NBSSI): Ɔman Adwumakuo a Ɛhwɛ Mfidinnwuma Nketewa so no yɛ ɔman adwumakuo a ɛnyɛ mfasoɔ enti na wɔwɔ hɔ na mmom, ɛyɛ adwumakuo a ɛhyɛ Asoɛeɛ a Ɛhwɛ Edwadie ne Mfidinnwuma so no ase, a mmara ma wɔn ho ɛkwan sɛ wɔnhwɛ sɛ Mfidinnwuma Nketewa ne Adantam (Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) bɛtu mpɔn.
english: MSME (Micro And Small Buisness Developmet Programme): A micro-enterprise (or microenterprise) is generally defined as a small business employing a minimum number of people, and having a balance sheet or turnover less than a certain amount NABCo (Nation Builders Corps): also known as NABCO is an initiative introduced by the Government of Ghana to provide jobs to unemployed university graduates to solve various social problems in both the private and public sectors and build their skills to promote economic growth in the country.

twi: Ɔman Nnuadua Dwumadie (National Afforestation Programme-NAP): Ɛyɛ kwaeɛ a yɛatɔre aseɛ no ananmuhyɛ sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a kwaeɛ mu nnepa a ahwere yɛn no bɛsane aba na ɛnam so ama mpɔtam ahodoɔ a wɔtete bɛn kwaeɛ, titire ahiafoɔ no asetenam atu mpɔn.
english: NBSSI (National Board For Small And Medium Scale Industry): The National Board for Small Scale Industries (NBSSI)

twi: 49 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ Ɔman Atoyerɛnkyɛm ho Ntotoeɛ Adwumakuo (National Disaster Management Organisation - NADMO): Yei yɛ ɔman adwumakuo a ɛhwɛ toto atoyerɛnkyɛm ne mpofirim asianeɛ ahodoɔ ho nsɛm wɔ ɔman Ghana mu.
english: Addition” 33 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget is a non-profit public sector organisation under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and is mandated to promote the growth and development of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs).

twi: Ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ bo a ɛsom a Fango Sika nka ho (Non-Oil Real GDP): Yei yɛ ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ nyinaa bo ɛsom a sika a ɛfiri fango ho dwumadie ahodoɔ mu nka ho bi, a wɔagyina nneɛma boɔ sorokɔ so no asese.
english: National Afforestation Programme (NAP): It is an ecological restoration of degraded forests and to develop the forest resources with peoples’ participation, with focus on improvement in livelihoods of the forest-fringe communities, especially the poor.

twi: Ɔman yi mu adwadeɛ bo a ɛsom kankorɔ a Fango Sika nka ho (Non-Oil Real GDP Growth): Ɛyɛ nnyinasoɔ a yɛhwɛ so de hunu ɔman sikasɛm mu mpontuo wɔ ɔman no nkorabata biara a fango sika nka ho bie.
english: National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO): It is the government agency that is responsible for the management of disasters as well as other emergencies in Ghana Non-Oil Real GDP: Is the total output in the economy that excludes the activities in the oil sector, which takes into account the level of inflation Non-Oil Real GDP Growth: It is an indicator that measures the real annual economic growth of all sectors except oil.

twi: Sika a ɛmfiri ɛtoɔ mu (Non Tax Revenue): Yei yɛ Aban sika a ɔnya a ɛmfiri ɛtoɔ mu. Ebi ne sika a obi tua ansa na wanya tumi krataa bi adi dwuma ne sika a yɛtua wɔ nneɛma afoforɔ ho sɛ ebia nsiho ne mfantum ho.
english: Non Tax Revenue: Government revenue not generated from taxes, examples are fees for granting permit or licenses, user fees and other charges.

twi: Ɛka Ahodoɔ A Aban De (Outstanding Obligations): Ɛka ahodoɔ a Aban de no yɛ sika a ɛsɛ sɛ Asoɛeɛ a Ɛhwɛ Sikasɛm so no tua ma Aban Nnwuma ahodoɔ no ɛnna afei, ɛka ɛda hɔ firi afe 2016 mu a mmara hyɛ sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ Aban tua gu Mmara ho Fotoɔ ahodoɔ mu.
english: Outstanding Obligations: The outstanding obligations comprise MDA commitments with the Ministry of Finance as well as outstanding 2016 payments to Statutory Funds.

twi: Nsunsuansoɔ (Outturn): Yei yɛ deɛ ɛsi wɔ tebea bi akyi anaa sɛ tebea ahodoɔ bi akyi.
english: Outturn: It is the result of a process or sequence of events.

twi: Sika Dodoɔ A Aka A Yɛbɛhia De Adi Dwuma (Primary balance): Yei yɛ sika dodoɔ a aka wɔ ɛberɛ a Aban agyegye deɛ n’ani da ɛkwan sɛ ɔbɛnya no nyinaa akyi de adi dwuma, a bosea ho nsiho nka ho bie, (kyerɛ sɛ bosea a Aban bɛtua nka ho).
english: Primary balance : This is the difference between Government revenue and its non interest expenditure (excluding debt Service Payment).

twi: Na ɛkwan a yɛfa so bu yei ho nkonta ne sɛ yɛsese no wɔ Ɔman Adwadeɛ nyinaa bo a ɛsom no mu ɔha mu nkyekyɛmu.
english: This can be measured as a percentage of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

twi: Sika a yɛadi aboro deɛ yɛwɔ so (Primary surplus - deficit): Yei kyerɛ sikasɛm mpɛmpɛnsoɔ a ɛgyina hɔ ma sika a yɛadi aboro deɛ yɛwɔ so a yɛagyegyeɛ afiri ɛtoɔ mu a, nsiho a yɛatua wɔ ɛka a ɔman no de nka ho.
english: Primary surplus (deficit): It refers to the component of the fiscal surplus (deficit) that is comprised of current government spending less current income from taxes, and excludes interest paid on government debt.

twi: 50 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ Ɔman mu Adwadeɛ nyinaa ankasa (Real GDP): Yei yɛ susudua a wɔde hunu ɔman mu adwadeɛ nyinaa bo a ɛsom a wɔde atoto sɛdeɛ nneɛma-boɔ-sorokɔ no teɛ ho.
english: Addition” 34 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget Projected Growth Rate: How the Ghanaian economy will grow in a year.

twi: Sika A Aban Nya (Revenue): Yei yɛ sika dodoɔ a Aban nya firi ne dwumadie ahodoɔ a ɔdi wɔ ɔman yi mu ne amannɔne.
english: Real GDP: It is a measure of a country's gross domestic product that has been adjusted for inflation Revenue: This is the total amount of money that Government receives for its activities from both domestic and external sources.

twi: Mmoayɛn A Ɛde Nnuane ne Nnwuma Ba -RFJ (Rearing For Food and Jobs): Yei yɛ Ghana Aban mpontuo ho dwumadie foforɔ a ɔde aba a ɛnam so bɛma ntɔtemmoayɛn adwuma no adi mu na sika aba mu sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ a, ntɔtemmoa nam bɛdɔɔso ama ɔmanfoɔ anya bi awe na yɛate ntɔtemmoa nam a yɛkra ba ɔman yi mu no so koraa, na ɛnam so ama nnwuma abu so a ɔmanfoɔ bɛnya bi ayɛ ama wɔn a wɔdi ntɔtemmoa ho dwuma nyinaa no asetenam nso atu mpɔn.
english: RFJ (Rearing For Food and Jobs): will develop a competitive and more efficient livestock industry, that will increase domestic production, reduce importation of livestock products, contribute to employment creation, and improve livelihoods of livestock value chain actors”.

twi: Nkyerɛkyerɛ a ɛde nsakraeɛ Ba (Sensitization): Yei yɛ nkyerɛkyerɛ anaa dawubɔ a ne botaeɛ ne sɛ ɛbɛma nhunumu ne adwenesakra nam so de nsakraeɛ pa aba tebea bi a ɛnyɛ mu.
english: Sensitization: The quality or condition of responding to certain stimuli in a sensitive manner.

twi: Nnwuma Nketewa ne Adantam (Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises - SMEs): TYeinom yɛ ankorankoro nnwuma a ɛnhyɛ aban ase a wɔtumi fa nnipa kakra bi de di wɔn dwuma. Asetena mu Mmoa Sika (Social Benefits): Yei yɛ sika a Aban gyina ɔmanfoɔ anan mu tua ma nsuo, pɛtro ne nkanea nnwumakuo no de sɔ Ghanafoɔ asene.
english: Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMEs): They are nonsubsidiary, independent firms that employ less than a given number of employees Social Benefits: Government pays subsidies to utility companies and on petroleum products on behalf of the public.

twi: Squadron: Yei yɛ ewiem asraafoɔ ekuo bi a wɔwɔ ewiemhyɛn a wɔde di wɔn dwuma no mmienu a anaa deɛ ɛboro saa ne asraafoɔ a ɛsɛ sɛ wɔka ewienhyɛn no.
english: Squadron: It is an operational unit in an air force consisting of two or more flights of aircraft and the personnel required to fly them.

twi: Asenesɔ Sika (Subsidy): Yei yɛ sika mu mmoa bi a Aban de ma ɔman mma ma ɛyi adesoa kakra firi wɔn so ma wɔn kɔn mu dwo wɔn.
english: Subsidy: This is a financial relief given by government to citizens to reduce the burden on them.

twi: Dwumadie akyiridie (Surveillance): Yei yɛ ɛkwan a yɛfa so de ani di biribi akyi na yɛhwɛ sɛdeɛ ɛsi teɛ.
english: Surveillance: The process of critically or intellectually observing an issue.

twi: Asorɔkye kunini (Tidal wave): Ɛyɛ ɛpo asorɔkye a ɛso pa ara a ɛba wɔ ɛberɛ a ɛpo ase asasewosoɔ bi asi anaa ɔbotan mu awosoɔ bi akɔ so wɔ ɛpo ase.
english: Tidal wave: It is an exceptionally large ocean wave, especially one caused by an underwater earthquake or volcanic eruption.

twi: Fannyɛ (Transparency): Yei ne sɛ Aban bɛma ɔman mma ahunu deɛ ɛrekɔ so na wɔate amanneɛbɔ nyinaa wɔ ɛberɛ ano ɛberɛ ano.
english: Transparency: This is when Government provides adequate and timely information for its citizens about what it is doing.

twi: Kwantempɔm (Trunk Road): Yei yɛ lɔre ɛkwan titire a mpn pii no ɛka nkuro mmienu anaa deɛ ɛboro saa, suhyɛn gyinabea, ewiemhyɛn gyinabea
english: Trunk Road: It is a major road, usually connecting two or more cities, ports, airports and other places, which is the recommended route for long-distance and freight traffic.

twi: 51 | Ghana Aban – 2023 Ɔman Mma Sikasɛm Nhyehyeɛ ne mmeaeɛ afoforɔ bom, na mpɛn pii no ɛyɛ ɛkwan tenten a yɛfa so de nneɛma kɔ akyirikyiri. Adwadeɛ ne Dwumadie ho sika (Use of Goods and Services): Yei yɛ sika dodoɔ a Aban tua wɔ dwuma a ɔdi ne dwumadie a ɔdi ma ɔmanfoɔ ho ho.
english: Addition” 35 | Government of Ghana - 2023 Citizens’ Budget Use of Goods and Services: Amount of money that Government pays for running its operations and for delivering services to the public.

twi: Adwadeɛ ho ɛtoɔ (Value Added Tax (VAT): Yei yɛ ɛtoɔ bi a yɛde to adwadeɛ ahodoɔ so wɔ adwadeɛyɛ mpɛmpɛnsoɔ biara mu.
english: Value Added Tax (VAT): The tax levied as value is added to goods and services at each stage of production.

twi: Mmɔborɔwafoɔ Aduonu (V20 - Vulnerable Twenty): Yeinom yɛ aman bi a wɔsusu sɛ ewiem nsakraeɛ ho nsuansuansoɔ a ano yɛ den no ka wɔn pa ara.
english: V20 (Vulnerable Twenty): They are detailed massive economic damage wrought by climate change on the economies representing countries considered the most vulnerable to climate change.

twi: Ɔman nkorabata (Subsector) – Ɛgyina hɔ ma ɔman no asoɛeɛ ahodoɔ no mu baako a dwumadie ahodoɔ kɔ so wɔ hɔ.
english: Subsector - an area of economic activity that forms part of one of the larger areas into which the economic activity of a country is divided.

twi: Wo-Deɛ-Hyɛ-Aseɛ (YouStart): Ɛyɛ ɛkwan a Aban pɛ sɛ ɔfa so boa mmabunu a wɔadi firi mfeɛ 18 kɔ 40 wɔ sikasɛm ne mfidie ho ma wɔde hyɛ wɔn nnwuma ase anaa sɛ nnwuma a ɛyɛ mmabunu dea na ɛnam so ama wɔahyɛ aseɛ na wɔatumi atrɛ wɔn ankasa nnwuma mu. Mmabunu Adwumanya ho Adwumakuo (Youth Employment Agency - YEA): Wɔnam mmara a ɛtɔ so ahanwɔtwe ne aduɔwɔtwe nson a ɛyɛ Mmabunu Adwumanya ho Mmara a wɔhyɛɛ no afe 2015 mu (Youth Employment Act 2015 - Act 887) no so buee Mmabunu Adwumanya ho Adwumakuo yi sɛdeɛ ɛbɛhwɛ ahyehyɛ, atoto, ahwɛ na waboa wɔ mmabunu adwumanya ne nsɛm a ɛfa wɔn ho wɔ Ghanaman mu.
english: YouStart: It is a vehicle through which Government intends to provide funding and technical support to youth (18-40) and youthled businesses who fall within this category to assist them start, build and grow their own businesses Youth Employment Agency (YEA): The YEA was established under the Youth Employment Act 2015 (Act 887), to oversee the development, coordination, supervision and facilitation of employment for the youth and related matters in Ghana
